decision_reason: This is a public GLPI escalation plugin maintained under an individual developer account; no government creation, commission, funding, or stewardship is evidenced. The French SILL entry is a recommendation listing, not provenance. The assigned repository's own license is AGPL-3.0-or-later, not the SILL metadata's GPL-2.0-only. Reject on government provenance; current product-level use/support evidence is also insufficient for admission.

government_provenance.note: The repository identifies author David Durieux and links to this personal maintainer's project; no agency, public commission, or grant is named. The SILL record is only a discovery/recommendation entry and does not establish government provenance.

eligible_license.note: The repository root LICENSE is the full GNU AGPL version 3 grant, and setup.php states AGPL v3 or any later version. This exact repository scope is AGPL-3.0-or-later; it conflicts with the SILL metadata label GPL-2.0-only. Third-party dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The plugin manifest describes an escalation add-on and links release downloads, but the repository has no evidenced current versioned release or qualifying production deployment/reuse. The last push was 2023-01-23 and the available social signals are limited; this does not prove abandonment, so status is unresolved.

decision_reason: The assigned URL is an organization pointer spanning multiple official Delta Chat clients and shared-core repositories, not one canonical code root with a single license scope. OTF's primary project page directly documents $502,870 in Delta Chat grants ($203,020 in 2018 and $299,850 in 2019); OTF's FY2017 report establishes that it was then an RFA program funded by an annual USAGM grant, while OTF only became an independent USAGM grantee in 2019. Public source, active official distribution, current product support, and product-specific notability are evidenced. Hold because the org-wide license and component/grant boundaries cannot be represented as one repository-level grant; coordinator should reconcile it as one product family and assign exact repo leads if needed.

government_provenance.note: OTF's official project record names Delta Chat and lists two direct awards, including 2018 and 2019 grants and their software-development purposes. OTF's FY2017 annual report states it was then an RFA program funded by USAGM; the 2019 independence announcement/USAGM history date its later independent-grantee status. This supports public funding of the product while avoiding retroactive characterization of OTF as independent in 2018.

public_source.note: The official Delta Chat GitHub organization exposes public Android, iOS, desktop, and shared-core repositories, but the assigned organization URL is not one source repository.

eligible_license.note: The official clients are public under distinct first-party grants: Android GPL-3.0-or-later, desktop GPL-3.0-or-later, iOS MPL-2.0, and current Chatmail Core MPL-2.0. These exact component texts are eligible licenses, but no single grant covers the organization pointer as a whole; optional Tauri and other components require separate scope checks.

primary_evidence.note: Official download/help pages support current product use; Delta Chat's 2025 product post reports substantial active onboarding and messaging traffic, the OTF-funded needfinding report is product-specific, and OTF/Cure53 published a security audit of the apps. These support current distribution/use and notability for the product family, not one repository's scope.

agency: Open Technology Fund (OTF); for 2018, OTF was a Radio Free Asia program supported by an annual U.S. Agency for Global Media grant; OTF became an independent USAGM grantee in 2019
geography: U.S. public funding relationship; product steward Merlinux GmbH in Freiburg, Germany; global user base
license: No organization-wide license. Checked first-party repositories include Android GPL-3.0-or-later, desktop GPL-3.0-or-later, iOS MPL-2.0, and current Chatmail Core MPL-2.0; scopes are repository/component-specific and dependencies retain their own terms.
family_note: The assigned https://github.com/deltachat URL is an organization pointer, not a repository. Official platform repos checked: https://github.com/deltachat/deltachat-android (GPL-3.0-or-later), https://github.com/deltachat/deltachat-desktop (GPL-3.0-or-later), https://github.com/deltachat/deltachat-ios (MPL-2.0), and current shared core https://github.com/chatmail/core (MPL-2.0; former deltachat-core-rust redirects here). The iOS and shared core grants differ from Android/desktop. The separate WIP Tauri edition and optional relays/dependencies are not included in this check. Coordinator should treat Delta Chat as one product family, not separate catalog entries for these components.
status_note: OTF's official Delta Chat project page lists two awards totaling $502,870 and describes development support. OTF's FY2017 annual report links its then-program status to RFA and an annual USAGM grant; OTF's 2019 announcement and USAGM history show the independent-grantee transition occurred later. The linked 2016-07-13 initial old-core commit contains the licensed project source, supporting a first public licensed-source year of 2016, but the old core is now deprecated and is not represented as the current core. Current official client repositories, download/help pages, the 2025 product post, and 2023 security audit support active status and notability. Held only for the organization-pointer/product-wide license-scope ambiguity; no catalog entry was added.
